# ========================================================================== # HioPoS -> Odoo | Gradual POS stock update during the day # -------------------------------------------------------------------------- # Model : pos.session # Type : Scheduled Action (ir.cron) # Ajustes > Tecnico > Automatizacion > Acciones planificadas # Interval : 10 Minutes | Priority: 20 | Repetir perdidos (doall): OFF # User : OdooBot # Odoo : 17.0 # Version : 17.0.1.0.0 # Sandbox : safe_eval compliant. No import / def / with / lambda / # comprehensions / getattr / attribute assignment. # -------------------------------------------------------------------------- # PURPOSE # The HioPoS fetch cron imports a large batch of orders every 25 minutes on # a fixed schedule that cannot be changed. With the company set to update # stock "at closing", no picking is created per order, so the entire stock # movement of the day lands in a single session close. # # This action performs that closing work in bounded slices during the day. # Each run it takes up to MAX_ORDERS_PER_RUN orders from the open sessions # in scope, groups their lines by destination location, and calls the SAME # standard helper the session close uses: # stock.picking._create_picking_from_pos_order_lines(dest, lines, type) # which creates the aggregated picking and validates it. Recipe components # are exploded by that helper, so combo products resolve correctly. # # Processed orders are then stamped with shipping_date, because # pos_session._create_picking_at_end_of_session() skips any order with one: # if order.company_id.anglo_saxon_accounting and order.is_invoiced # or order.shipping_date: # continue # That stamp is the entire anti duplication mechanism. Do not remove it. # -------------------------------------------------------------------------- # KNOWN RISK (accepted, not mitigated here) # The aggregated picking groups several orders, so it cannot carry # pos_order_id, and pos.order.picking_ids stays empty. The guard # "if self.picking_ids: return" in _create_order_picking therefore does not # protect these orders. If one is invoiced after the fact, # action_pos_order_invoice() reaches "if self.shipping_date:" and launches # stock rules, DUPLICATING the movement. Orders with to_invoice already set # are excluded up front; the exposure is only manual post hoc invoicing of # a POS ticket, which must be avoided on the configs in scope. # # KNOWN LIMITATION # A destination group that always fails is rebuilt identically on every run # and blocks its queue. The failing order names are logged for that reason. # If it happens, fix the underlying record; there is no automatic split. # -------------------------------------------------------------------------- # DEPLOYMENT CHECKLIST # [ ] POS_CONFIG_IDS filled with PRODUCTION ids (test ids are different) # [ ] FETCH_CRON_ID filled with the ir.cron id of "HioPoS: Fetch Orders" # [ ] Verified res.company.point_of_sale_update_stock_quantities = 'closing' # [ ] Verified a session close produces NO second picking for stamped orders # [ ] Dry run in production, log inspected # [ ] MAX_ORDERS_PER_RUN ramped 10 -> 50 -> target, watching the log # ==========================================================================
# -------------------- BLOQUE 0: CONSTANTES -------------------------------- # Dry run guard. Keep False for the first production run: the ids below are # environment specific and running blind with the wrong ones moves stock. EXECUTE = True
# POS configs in scope. REQUIRED: the action refuses to run when empty, so a # misconfiguration can never sweep every point of sale in the database. # A bare int is accepted for the single POS case: [73] and 73 both work. POS_CONFIG_IDS = [78]
# Orders processed per run, across all sessions in scope. # This is the only real load control: a destination group cannot be # interrupted once the standard helper is called. MAX_ORDERS_PER_RUN = 50
# Stop starting new groups once this many seconds have elapsed. TIME_BUDGET_SECONDS = 40
# Ignore orders younger than this, so the import transaction settles first. MIN_AGE_MINUTES = 2
# Only these session states are touched. 'closing_control' is excluded on # purpose: the close is already running and would race with this action. SESSION_STATES = ['opened']
# Cron ids to yield to while they hold their row lock. Add EVERY cron that # writes the same pos.order / pos.session / stock.quant rows, otherwise their # concurrent writes surface as PostgreSQL 40001 serialization failures. # Known writers: "HioPoS: Fetch Orders" and "HioPoS: Check Cierre Z". # Empty list = no probe at all (and busy_cron below stays 0, not proof of # an idle system). PAUSE_WHILE_CRON_IDS = [182, 183]
VERBOSE = True
# True = write to ir.logging only when something needs attention. # False = log every run, including clean ones. Flip to False while debugging. # A clean run leaves no log line, so traceability of what was moved lives in # the picking (origin = session name) and in FIELD_PICKING on each order. LOG_ONLY_ON_WARNING = True
# Studio Many2one on pos.order pointing at stock.picking, written so each # order links to the aggregated picking that moved its stock. Set to '' to # disable. VERIFY the technical name in Studio: auto generated fields look # like x_studio_many2one_field_XXXXX, not like the label you gave them. # Refund note: an order with both sale and refund lines produces two # pickings; a Many2one can only hold one, so the sale picking wins. FIELD_PICKING = 'x_studio_stockpicking'
# -------------------- BLOQUE 1: GUARD DE CONFIGURACION -------------------- # Normalise to a list: a domain 'in' term requires one, and writing a bare # int here is the natural mistake when there is a single POS in scope. config_ids = POS_CONFIG_IDS if isinstance(config_ids, int): config_ids = [config_ids]
config_ok = True if not config_ids: config_ok = False log( 'HIOPOS DAY SLICE ABORTED: POS_CONFIG_IDS is empty. Fill it with the ' 'production pos.config ids before enabling this action.', level='warning', )
# -------------------- BLOQUE 2: PAUSA SI EL FETCH ESTA CORRIENDO ---------- # Same mechanism Odoo uses to claim a cron job: try to lock its row. The # lock is always released via ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT, so this probe can never # block the cron it is checking. crons_busy = 0
if config_ok: for cron_id in PAUSE_WHILE_CRON_IDS: env.cr.execute('SAVEPOINT hiopos_probe') try: env.cr.execute( 'SELECT id FROM ir_cron WHERE id = %s FOR NO KEY UPDATE NOWAIT', (cron_id,), ) except Exception: crons_busy = crons_busy + 1 env.cr.execute('ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT hiopos_probe') env.invalidate_all(flush=False)
# -------------------- BLOQUE 3: SESIONES CANDIDATAS ----------------------- t_start = datetime.datetime.utcnow() cutoff_str = (t_start - datetime.timedelta(minutes=MIN_AGE_MINUTES)).strftime( '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S' ) today_str = t_start.strftime('%Y-%m-%d')
Session = env['pos.session'] Order = env['pos.order'] Picking = env['stock.picking']
# Fail soft if the Studio field was renamed or not created yet: the stock # work must not stop because a traceability field is missing. has_picking_field = False if FIELD_PICKING: if FIELD_PICKING in Order._fields: has_picking_field = True
sessions = Session if config_ok: if crons_busy < 1: sessions = Session.search( [('state', 'in', SESSION_STATES), ('config_id', 'in', config_ids)], order='id asc', )
# -------------------- BLOQUE 4: PROCESO POR SESION ------------------------ budget_left = MAX_ORDERS_PER_RUN count_orders = 0 count_pickings = 0 count_pending = 0 count_fail = 0 skipped_realtime = 0 stopped_on_time = False # A 40001 leaves this transaction on a stale snapshot: retrying the same work # here fails again deterministically, so the whole run is abandoned and the # next scheduled run picks it up with a fresh snapshot. aborted_conflict = False plan_log = '' created_log = '' failed_log = '' last_error = ''
for session in sessions: if budget_left < 1: break
if aborted_conflict: break
elapsed = (datetime.datetime.utcnow() - t_start).total_seconds() if elapsed > TIME_BUDGET_SECONDS: stopped_on_time = True break
# Hard guard: in real time mode the standard flow already created a # picking per order, and slicing here would double count the stock. if not session.update_stock_at_closing: skipped_realtime = skipped_realtime + 1 continue
picking_type = session.config_id.picking_type_id if not picking_type: continue
# Same fallback the standard close uses when the type has no destination. if picking_type.default_location_dest_id: session_destination_id = picking_type.default_location_dest_id.id else: session_destination_id = env['stock.warehouse']._get_partner_locations()[0].id
# to_invoice orders are excluded: under anglo saxon accounting they build # their own picking, and they are the post hoc invoicing exposure. orders = Order.search( [ ('session_id', '=', session.id), ('state', 'not in', ['draft', 'cancel']), ('shipping_date', '=', False), ('to_invoice', '=', False), ('date_order', '<=', cutoff_str), ], order='id asc', limit=budget_left, ) if not orders: continue
# ---- Group lines and orders by destination location ------------------- lines_by_dest = {} orders_by_dest = {} for order in orders: # property_stock_customer is company dependent: read it with the # session company active or it resolves against the wrong company. partner = order.partner_id.with_company(session.company_id.id) dest_id = partner.property_stock_customer.id or session_destination_id if dest_id in lines_by_dest: lines_by_dest[dest_id] = lines_by_dest[dest_id] | order.lines orders_by_dest[dest_id] = orders_by_dest[dest_id] | order else: lines_by_dest[dest_id] = order.lines orders_by_dest[dest_id] = order
plan_log = ( plan_log + ' | ' + session.name + ': ' + str(len(orders)) + ' orders / ' + str(len(lines_by_dest)) + ' dest' )
if not EXECUTE: budget_left = budget_left - len(orders) count_orders = count_orders + len(orders) continue
# ---- One savepoint per destination group ------------------------------ for dest_id in lines_by_dest: if aborted_conflict: break
elapsed = (datetime.datetime.utcnow() - t_start).total_seconds() if elapsed > TIME_BUDGET_SECONDS: stopped_on_time = True break
savepoint = 'hiopos_slice_' + str(session.id) + '_' + str(dest_id) env.cr.execute('SAVEPOINT ' + savepoint) try: group_lines = lines_by_dest[dest_id] group_orders = orders_by_dest[dest_id]
# Golden rule: act with the session company active so accounts, # taxes and locations resolve against the right company. target = Picking.with_company(session.company_id.id).with_context( allowed_company_ids=[session.company_id.id], skip_sms=True, )
# Standard helper: creates the aggregated picking, explodes recipe # components and calls _action_done() inside its own savepoint. It # swallows UserError on missing stock and leaves it unvalidated. pickings = target._create_picking_from_pos_order_lines( dest_id, group_lines, picking_type )
if pickings: # Mirror what the session close writes, so the picking hangs # off the session and cost computation finds its moves. pickings.write({ 'pos_session_id': session.id, 'origin': session.name, })
# The stamp that makes the night close skip these orders. order_vals = {'shipping_date': today_str}
if has_picking_field: if pickings: # Prefer the sale picking: with refunds the helper also # returns a return picking, and a Many2one holds one. main_picking = pickings[0] for pk in pickings: if pk.picking_type_id.id == picking_type.id: main_picking = pk break order_vals[FIELD_PICKING] = main_picking.id
group_orders.write(order_vals)
# Writes are buffered: flush inside the try so a database error # lands in this except block and not in the next group. env.flush_all()
for pk in pickings: created_log = created_log + ' | ' + str(pk.name) + ':' + str(pk.state) if pk.state == 'done': count_pickings = count_pickings + 1 else: count_pending = count_pending + 1
count_orders = count_orders + len(group_orders) env.cr.execute('RELEASE SAVEPOINT ' + savepoint)
except Exception as err: env.cr.execute('ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT ' + savepoint) # invalidate_all() calls flush_all() internally, which would # replay the rolled back writes: always flush=False here. env.invalidate_all(flush=False)
count_fail = count_fail + 1 message = str(err) if len(message) > 400: message = message[:400] last_error = session.name + '/' + str(dest_id) + ': ' + message
# Name the blocked orders: this group is rebuilt identically next # run, so a human has to look at them. for order in orders_by_dest[dest_id]: failed_log = failed_log + ' ' + str(order.name)
# PostgreSQL 40001. The connection survives the savepoint # rollback, but the snapshot does not: stop the run instead of # burning the remaining groups on guaranteed failures. if 'could not serialize' in message: aborted_conflict = True if 'concurrent update' in message: aborted_conflict = True
budget_left = budget_left - len(orders)
# -------------------- BLOQUE 5: RESUMEN ----------------------------------- # A run is worth logging when it failed, hit a conflict, left a picking # unvalidated, found a session in real time mode, or lost the Studio field. # Clean runs and idle runs stay silent. worth_logging = False if count_fail: worth_logging = True if aborted_conflict: worth_logging = True if count_pending: worth_logging = True if skipped_realtime: worth_logging = True if FIELD_PICKING: if not has_picking_field: worth_logging = True
should_log = False if VERBOSE: if config_ok: if worth_logging: should_log = True if not LOG_ONLY_ON_WARNING: should_log = True
if should_log: level = 'info' if worth_logging: level = 'warning' prefix = 'HIOPOS DAY SLICE' if not EXECUTE: prefix = 'HIOPOS DAY SLICE [DRY RUN]' log( prefix + ' busy_cron=' + str(crons_busy) + ' configs=' + str(len(config_ids)) + ' probes=' + str(len(PAUSE_WHILE_CRON_IDS)) + ' picking_field=' + str(has_picking_field) + ' conflict_abort=' + str(aborted_conflict) + ' sessions=' + str(len(sessions)) + ' orders=' + str(count_orders) + ' pickings_done=' + str(count_pickings) + ' pickings_pending=' + str(count_pending) + ' groups_failed=' + str(count_fail) + ' skipped_realtime=' + str(skipped_realtime) + ' time_capped=' + str(stopped_on_time) + ' plan=' + plan_log + ' created=' + created_log + ' blocked_orders=' + failed_log + ' last_error=' + last_error, level=level, )
